reader.title: Killing of Frank Matterson and two horse thieves at Rock Creek
chips: Lynching of any race (not in the anti-Black count)
bases: A1 says that three men accused of stealing horses were overtaken after a search, that one was shot dead and the other two 'were hung', with no court or officer mentioned.

A1 reports three accused horse thieves killed (one shot, two hanged) after a pursuit, with no lawful process mentioned and the killings framed as revenge for the thefts; the killers are not named or counted, and the account is hearsay ('it is said') from a single report.
Only A1, a brief item in the Cheyenne Daily Leader resting on 'it is said', reports the killings; no second report was found.

summary.text: The killing of Frank Matterson and two horse thieves at Rock Creek was the reported shooting of Matterson, called "Big Frank", and the hanging of two unnamed men, all three accused of stealing horses in North Park, in about June 1881.
The only known account, a brief item in the Cheyenne Daily Leader, rested on hearsay and said the people of the park felt "justly revenged."
According to the Leader, horse thieves had run off "a large number of horses" in North Park a month or six weeks before its June 24 issue.
Indignation "ran very high," and it was reported that the thieves would be "strung up" immediately if they were caught.
A search was made for them, though it was generally supposed they would never be captured.
The thieves, three in number, were "said" to have been overtaken recently at Rock Creek.
Frank Matterson was shot dead, and the other two men, whose names "could not be ascertained," were hanged.
The item does not say who overtook them, how many pursuers there were, or whether anyone watched, and it gives no date, time or county.
The men reportedly had about forty head of stolen horses with them when captured.
No report of an inquest, arrest or other official response appears in the coverage, and the race of the three men is not stated.
The Cheyenne Daily Leader ran the story on June 24, 1881, as a short front-page item headed "Captured."

It called the thefts "nefarious games," attributed the killings to hearsay with "it is said," and closed by saying the people of the park "undoubtedly feel justly revenged," presenting the killings as deserved.
No other paper's account of the killings appears in the coverage.
